# Decisions log

Rulings made by Marcel on what the transcript findings should change. Recorded so they are not
re-litigated. Evidence for each sits in `FINDINGS.md`.

**Working rule, set 2026-08-30:** nothing lands unapproved. Any change to a skill or agent —
structural or textual — is presented as a proposal with its rationale and waits for an explicit go.

**Framing that governs all of these:** the transcripts record what happened, and a fair amount of
what happened was the failure mode, not the method. They are a source to learn from, not a spec to
transcribe. A finding earns a place in a skill only if it makes future work better — not because
it is what was done before.

---

## Applied — 2026-08-30

### `skills/zimmerMANNPreBuild/SKILL.md`
| Change | Why |
|---|---|
| One Figma node URL per variant **and** state, not per component | You routinely supply 3–4; one node hides the states where defects live |
| Archived-vs-current design triage | An archived node that still renders is a trap; you check this by hand today |
| Measurement traps: TEXT reports a cap-height box (not comparable to a CSS line box), FRAMES/INSTANCES are; never cross-compare the two Figma files | Both produced real false defects |
| "No design is a blocker, not licence to invent" — or an explicit provisional carried as an assumption | *"it's in the ACs but not in the designs, do we agree on that?"* |
| Provenance, not proximity — flag "provenance unknown" rather than fabricate a source | Your own CRITICAL RULE #2 |
| Local-only docs never citable in a PR, commit or code comment | *"it's wrong to mention the fed lead playbook here, because that file is only local to me"* |
| Scale to the work; `quick` depth names what it drops | *"scaled appropriately to the need, nothing too crazy, no overthinking"* |
| ELI5-but-FED-Lead register on output | Asked for 60+ times across the corpus |
| Decisions presented one at a time **via AskUserQuestion** | *"ask me one-by-one"* — and your explicit instruction to use the tool for it |
| Explicit handoff gate — the skill presents and stops, never invokes Build | Discover → report → approve → execute is your standing contract |

### `agents/zm-planner.md`
| Change | Why |
|---|---|
| The scale call must be **stated and defended** — how much loop the work warrants, with over-scaled machinery named as a defect in the plan | Right-sizing must be visible and challengeable, not inferred independently by each agent |

---

## Held — ruled, not yet written

Deliberately not applied while the agents they belong to are unwired. Apply when the owning skill
is built.

### For `zimmerMANNBuild` (Skill #2) — `zm-orchestrator`
- **UNDER and OVER become equal-weight peer verdicts.** Remove the "over-delivery is the one that
  gets missed" lean. *"does it fully fulfil the requirements **and no less**?"*

### For `zimmerMANNBuild` (Skill #2) — `zm-scorer`
- **Six axes**, not five: Pass criteria · Correctness · **Design fidelity** · Conformance ·
  Completeness · Restraint. Design fidelity gets its own PASS/REWORK — the `width: 'xl'` bug
  passed tsc, eslint, vitest, CodeRabbit and Storybook a11y, and only a human eye caught it.
- **A PASS must state what was attacked and how the work survived.** No falsification attempt,
  no PASS.
- **Required "What I could not verify" section.**
- Findings labelled **CONFIRMED** (reproduced) or **PLAUSIBLE** (reasoned, unproven).

### For `zimmerMANNBuild` (Skill #2) — `zm-tester`
- Same falsification requirement and **"What I could not verify"** section.
- Every finding tagged **UNIFORM** or **ONE-OFF** — could this defect shape repeat across the
  feature's other files? Per-step scoring is structurally blind to uniform divergence; a
  systematic spacing error once survived five commits and every score.
- **CONFIRMED / PLAUSIBLE** labelling.

### For `zimmerMANNPostBuild` (Skill #3)
- **A whole-feature sweep before the PR** — "does the whole feature match what the exemplar
  established?" This is the only thing that catches a pattern applied consistently but wrongly.

### For `zimmerMANNReview` (Skill #4) and `zimmerMANNPostBuild`
- **Decision-owner column** on findings, plus the phrasing rule: where the owner is senior or
  lateral, phrase the finding as a question to them, never a directive. *"DO NOT DIRECT TIM, ASK
  HIM CONFIRMATORILY"*. Deferred out of PreBuild — it matters where outward-facing text is written.

### Cross-cutting
- **Scale rule in every skill**, alongside the planner's justification of the scale it chose.

| Proposal | Ruling |
|---|---|
| **Prove-before-build** as a stage, an agent, or a plan section | *"prove-by-execution only adds work that is equivalent to what we'll do during build → build, test, address if needed; it's redundant and wasteful."* The footer session's prove-stage existed because it was **auditing an existing branch**. Building fresh, build→test→address covers the same ground in one pass. |
| **Yield-floor stop rule** (halt when a pass drops below ~20% behaviour+correctness) | Round cap only. One number to watch; the yield calculation is itself a judgement that could go wrong. |
| **Decision-owner column in PreBuild** | Belongs in Review and PostBuild, where things get sent to people. Not in a planning gate that writes nothing public. |
| **Anchor text alongside `file:line`** | CONFIRMED/PLAUSIBLE only. Line drift is caught when someone opens the file anyway. |
| **Distrust-the-brief** and the **instruction-refusal protocol** | Too much latitude for an agent. Catching a wrong brief is the Tester's and Scorer's job downstream, not something the Implementer acts on unilaterally. |
| **A seventh agent (`zm-prover`)** | Created without approval on 2026-08-30, removed the same day. Superseded by the prove-before-build ruling above. |

## Applied — 2026-08-30, Skill #2 `zimmerMANNBuild`

### Design rulings
| Decision | Ruling |
|---|---|
| Loop shape | **Return path**, as PDP Static ran it — Implementer → Tester → Orchestrator → Scorer → REWORK back to Implementer, max 3 rounds. Not the footer's linear pipeline. |
| Who commits | **Build commits per step; PostBuild pushes and opens the PR.** Resolves the conflict between the original spec (PostBuild does all three) and what PDP Static actually ran. The *skill* commits, never an agent. |
| Rework entry | **A second mode inside `zimmerMANNBuild`** — `build` and `rework`. Not a separate skill, not folded into PostBuild. |

The review then completed: a `Request changes` verdict plus 11 line-cited inline comments, drafted and parked on *"Nothing posts until you say go."* Your go never came, because you'd never asked for a review. **13 findings, 0 posted, 3 of them execution-proven shopper-facing bugs** — roughly 90 minutes and ~2.5M subagent tokens for zero output, on a PR that merged four days later approved by others.

Not a detection failure. The audit worked. It's a trigger problem: nothing in the skill distinguishes "investigate this PR's CI failure" from "review this PR."

- PR #83 was ~425 lines of unique work, not 724 — `de149822` is a byte-identical replay of `9ae445e0` forked to re-ask one question, not a second review.

content.content:
---
name: zimmerMANNReview
description: Reviews someone else's PR as FED Lead. Establishes ground truth, fans out audit angles, verifies every finding before it is raised, then presents for adjudication — Marcel decides the verdict, and comments post only on his go. Loops until the PR is approved.
---

Review of a colleague's work. Same architecture as the build chain — ground truth, a gated audit,
then present and stop — tailored to a PR you did not write.

**Intended model: Sonnet 5 at maximum effort.**

**The thing that makes it work:** you hold the ground truth and the adjudication, and delegate only
the reading. Reviewers are cheap and fallible; measurements are expensive and authoritative. Keep
those on opposite sides of the line.

**Input:** `$ARGUMENTS` — a PR number.

**Scale to the work.** A two-file PR does not get four reviewers. Nothing too crazy, no
overthinking.

---

## Phase 1 — ground truth. Yours, not an agent's.

### Frame the PR

Base SHA, head SHA, files changed, ±lines. **Use the live head** — a stale ref has already caused a
whole round of re-verification here.

### Requirements — Jira, Confluence, Figma

Build the same requirements picture a PreBuild would build, then judge the PR against it. Every
scope argument, every "this is missing", every "this wasn't asked for" gets decided against these
words — not the PR description's paraphrase of them.

**Jira.** Pull the full ticket: description, ACs, linked work items, and — critically — the full
comment thread. Decisions made in comments routinely contradict the description and never make it
back into the ACs. Flag: untestable ACs · requirements that contradict each other or the comments
· a linked blocker still open · a decision in comments that the implementation may not have seen ·
**evidence that a different PR, branch, or assignee is already working the same ticket.**

description: Reviews someone else's PR as FED Lead. Establishes ground truth, fans out audit angles, verifies every finding before it is raised, then presents for adjudication — Marcel decides the verdict, and comments post only on his go. Loops until the PR is approved.
---

Review of a colleague's work. Same architecture as the build chain — ground truth, a gated audit,
then present and stop — tailored to a PR you did not write.

**Intended model: Sonnet 5 at maximum effort.**

**The thing that makes it work:** you hold the ground truth and the adjudication, and delegate only
the reading. Reviewers are cheap and fallible; measurements are expensive and authoritative. Keep
those on opposite sides of the line.

**Input:** `$ARGUMENTS` — a PR number.

**Scale to the work.** A two-file PR does not get four reviewers. Nothing too crazy, no
overthinking.

---

## Phase 1 — ground truth. Yours, not an agent's.

### Frame the PR

Base SHA, head SHA, files changed, ±lines. **Use the live head** — a stale ref has already caused a
whole round of re-verification here.

### Requirements — Jira, Confluence, Figma

Build the same requirements picture a PreBuild would build, then judge the PR against it. Every
scope argument, every "this is missing", every "this wasn't asked for" gets decided against these
words — not the PR description's paraphrase of them.

**Jira.** Pull the full ticket: description, ACs, linked work items, and — critically — the full
comment thread. Decisions made in comments routinely contradict the description and never make it
back into the ACs. Flag: untestable ACs · requirements that contradict each other or the comments
· a linked blocker still open · a decision in comments that the implementation may not have seen ·
**evidence that a different PR, branch, or assignee is already working the same ticket.**

## Verified live right now, found by your reviews, never posted

**1. `ZimmModal` never got the `__css` → `sx` fix that `ZimmDrawer` got in the same PR** — [zimmModal/index.tsx:86-87](overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmModal/index.tsx:86). Both `ModalOverlay` and `ModalContent` still use `__css`; `ZimmDrawer` uses `sx` at lines 149/152/160/210. I have the last sweep still out, but it only affects one Rev proposal's framing. The Dev side's top finding is ready and it outranks everything else in this exercise.

## PROPOSAL D1 — `skills/zimmerMANNBuild/SKILL.md`

**Gap:** brief · **Recurrence:** both builds in the window, plus a third instance on 5 Sep

**Evidence.** Across SFCC-83+84 (8–10 Sep, 40 commits, 16,869 lines), every `Agent` dispatch by type: `zm-implementer` 1, `zm-tester` 2, `zm-orchestrator` 2, **`zm-scorer` 0**. The loop `Implementer → Tester → Orchestrator → Scorer` completed **zero times**, and all 40 commits landed with no Scorer PASS — against this skill's own line 104: *"Only after: Scorer PASS."* On SFCC-236 the loop ran in full **once in thirteen** Implementer dispatches, with `zm-orchestrator` never dispatched at all.

Three things make this the root finding rather than one of many:

1. **The agent that never runs is the one holding the rule that would have caught the dominant defect class.** `zm-scorer.md` says design fidelity *"cannot be inferred from green gates."* The flush-geometry saga closed four separate times on *"Gates clean: tsc, tests, lint, token audit"* — and took **nine human-verdict rounds**, ending only when you demanded a browser check.
2. **It is invisible from inside.** The model diagnosed its own collapse mid-build — *"I've been running the whole loop as one undifferentiated agent — implementing, testing, judging my own scope, and calling it done"* — and then continued for two more days.
3. **Reloading the skill does not fix it.** The full text, including the handoff template, was loaded verbatim twice. One step entered the loop and was abandoned 46 minutes later: *"all built inline as agreed."*

The consequence is that you became the rework loop. Six instances of source-reading passed off as behavioural verification, every one caught by you or by CI, none by a gate.

**Current** (lines 104–105):
```
**The skill commits, not an agent.** Only after: Scorer PASS, and the visual checkpoint passed if
one was owed.
```

**Proposed:**
```
**The skill commits, not an agent.** Only after: Scorer PASS, and the visual checkpoint passed if
one was owed.

**State the provenance in the commit turn, or do not commit.** Name the step, which loop agents
actually ran for it, the Scorer's verdict and round, and the visual checkpoint's outcome. Any of
those that did not happen is written as **"did not run"** in those words — and a commit carrying
`did not run` against the Scorer, or against an owed visual checkpoint, stops for Marcel's
explicit override instead of proceeding. The loop collapsing into one inline agent is the most
expensive failure this skill has: it is invisible from inside, and re-reading this file mid-build
does not restore it. Only a per-commit statement makes it visible while it is still happening.
```

**Why:** it puts the check at the one point the skill actually controls — it owns the commit — and it makes the collapse a thing you'd see on commit one instead of on day three.

---
name: zimmerMANNBuild
description: The builder. Executes an approved zimmerMANNPreBuild plan through a closed-loop multi-agent workflow — implement, test, scope-check, score, rework until passed — committing each step and handing off to zimmerMANNPostBuild. Also handles rework from CodeRabbit or reviewer change requests after a PR is open.
---

The executor. Takes an approved plan and builds it, one step at a time, with every step tested,
scope-checked, scored and seen by Marcel before it becomes a commit.

**Intended model: Sonnet 5 at maximum effort.** A skill cannot pin the session model — the loop
agents are pinned to Sonnet in their own frontmatter regardless.

**Scale to the work.** A two-point story does not get the full loop. The plan states the scale it
chose and why; honour it. Over-scaled machinery is a defect, not thoroughness. Nothing too crazy,
no overthinking.

---

## Two modes

**`build`** — `$ARGUMENTS` is a Jira key. Reads `~/Dev/zimmerMANN-skills/.runs/<TICKET>/plan.md`
and executes it. This is the default.

**`rework`** — invoked as `rework <TICKET>` after a PR is open and CodeRabbit or a reviewer has
requested changes. Skips planning entirely; see the last section.

If no plan exists for the ticket, stop and say so. **Do not plan here** — that is
`zimmerMANNPreBuild`'s job, and building from an unplanned story is how an afternoon gets burned
on the wrong thing.

---

## Before the first step

1. Confirm the branch. **Not `develop`, not `main`** — a `PreToolUse` hook blocks every Write and
   Edit there. If the branch is wrong, stop.
2. Confirm the working tree is clean, or that everything dirty is expected and belongs to this
   story. Registry churn under `.claude/registry/*.md` is automatic and expected.
3. Read the plan's file manifest, tiers and per-step pass criteria. **Any file marked BLOCKED
   stops the run** until Marcel confirms owner approval.
4. Record the baseline: run the four per-step gates now and note the numbers. A gate that is
   non-zero at baseline is not a failure you introduced.

---

## The loop — once per step

```
Implementer  →  Tester  →  Orchestrator  →  Scorer  →  [Marcel]  →  commit
                   ↑                          │
                   └────── REWORK, max 3 ─────┘
```

**1. `zm-implementer`** builds the step. Only the files the step names. It never stages and never
commits.

**2. `zm-tester`** fans out its own angle sub-agents, re-pointed for this step, and reports
findings with CONFIRMED/PLAUSIBLE and UNIFORM/ONE-OFF labels, plus what it tried to falsify and
what it could not verify.

**3. `zm-orchestrator`** returns a scope verdict — IN SCOPE / UNDER / OVER / BLOCKED. Under and
over carry equal weight.

**4. `zm-scorer`** takes both and scores six axes. PASS or REWORK.

**REWORK returns to the Implementer with a specific instruction. Maximum three rounds.** On the
third, stop and surface to Marcel — three failures means the plan or the criteria are wrong, not
the implementation.

### Per-step gates — the cheap four

Run every step. Seconds each.

```
npx tsc --noEmit
npm run test                        # includes recipeGuards, the hard styling gate
npm run lint                        # compare counts, not the exit code
node scripts/auditTokenUsage.mjs    # new unacknowledged findings only
```

Two traps: `npm run lint` exits non-zero at a healthy baseline, so **compare the count against
your baseline and ignore the exit code**. And never append arguments to it — `pwa-kit-dev lint`
forwards `--`-args into `execSync`, which can silently turn the gate into a writer.

The plan's per-step pass criteria layer **on top of** these, they do not replace them.

### The visual checkpoint

**After any step that changes rendered output, the loop stops.** The plan marks which steps those
are; if it doesn't, assume any step touching a component, a recipe or a page does.

Tell Marcel exactly:
- the URL and the viewport to open
- the Figma node to compare against — the one for **that variant and state**
- what should be on screen
- what would indicate a defect, including anything that will look wrong but is correct

Then **wait.** Do not proceed on assumption. This is the only gate on this stack that catches a
layout defect — `width: 'xl'` passed every automated check and destroyed the global footer.

Until it has happened, the Scorer's Design fidelity axis is UNVERIFIED, not passed.

### The commit

**The skill commits, not an agent.** Only after: Scorer PASS, and the visual checkpoint passed if
one was owed.

One step, one commit. Conventional Commits — the `commit-msg` hook enforces it. **No Claude
attribution, no CodeRabbit mentions, no `Co-Authored-By` line.** Use Marcel's previously authored
commits on this repo as the reference for tone and body.

Then move to the next step.

---

## Before handing off

Once every step has passed, run the expensive gates **once**:

```
npm run build-storybook             # then run the interaction + a11y suite against it
npm run test:story                  # real BrowserStack, scoped to the Jira key
npm run test:max-file-size          # runs a full build
cr review --base develop            # CodeRabbit locally, full review before anything is public
```

Storybook needs a verified-free port and a build you can prove is yours — a stale server on 6006
produced a silently meaningless pass once. Check the served build matches your own before trusting
any result.

Then **write the handoff** to `~/Dev/zimmerMANN-skills/.runs/<TICKET>/handoff.md`:

```
# Handoff — <TICKET>
Branch: <branch>   Base: <sha>   Head: <sha>

## Steps
| # | What | Commit | Scorer verdict | Rework rounds |

## Gates (real numbers, not claims)
| Gate | Result | Baseline |

## UNIFORM findings
<each one, with file:line — these are what a per-step review structurally cannot catch>

## Could not verify
<named, with why>

## Outstanding
<anything left, or "none">
```

**Write it even when everything passed.** PostBuild reads this file, and it may run in a different
session — a handoff that exists only in conversation does not survive the session ending.

Then present the same content to Marcel and **hand off to `zimmerMANNPostBuild`. This skill does
not push and does not open a PR.**

---

## Rework mode

Entered after a PR is open and CodeRabbit or a reviewer has requested changes.

**Read `~/Dev/zimmerMANN-skills/.runs/<TICKET>/postbuild.md` first.** It records what earlier rounds
already declined and why. A finding that was declined with evidence in round one does not get
re-litigated in round three — check before you verify anything, and if you disagree with a previous
decline, say so rather than silently reversing it.

**1. Verify every finding before touching anything.** CodeRabbit has been wrong on this repo
often — one batch ran 1-in-6 correct. Treat each finding as a hypothesis, not a fact. Per finding:

- **VALID** — reproduce it, cite `file:line`, fix it
- **INVALID** — say what is actually true, with the evidence, and draft the reply
- **OUT OF SCOPE** — real but not this story's problem; name the owning ticket or the person
- **DEFER** — real, in scope, but blocked on a decision; name who decides

**2. Fix only the VALID ones.** Same rules as build mode — the Implementer touches only what the
finding names, never stages, never commits.

**3. Re-run the cheap four**, plus the visual checkpoint if the fix changes rendered output.

**4. Commit the fixes here**, same rule as build mode — the skill commits, never an agent. Reference
the review thread each commit answers.

**5. Hand back to `zimmerMANNPostBuild`** with: what was fixed and in which commit, what was
declined and why, and the evidence behind each decline. **PostBuild owns the push and the
in-thread replies** — every finding gets a written answer, including the declined ones.

---

## Hard rules

- **Never push. Never open or update a PR.** That boundary belongs to PostBuild, which presents
  first and pushes only once Marcel has given the go.
- **Never write to the repo's config** — `.claude/**`, `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `CODEOWNERS`,
  `.docs/memory/**`, `.docs/prd/**`. Tier 1 Governance.
- **Never touch a Tier 1 file** without Marcel naming it and confirming owner approval.
- **Never expand scope.** Something worth doing that the plan didn't ask for gets reported, not
  done. Report it and let Marcel decide.
- **Local-only docs are never citable** in a commit message or a code comment. Cite `AGENTS.md`
  or `.claude/rules/*` instead.
- **Say what you could not verify.** Silence reads as "nothing wrong" when it may mean
  "didn't look there".

D1 is in. Now the top Rev proposal — and the PR #65 sweep changed its shape, so this is not the one I drafted earlier.

## PROPOSAL R1 — `skills/zimmerMANNReview/SKILL.md`

**Gap:** Job C process · **Recurrence:** three of the four PRs reviewed in the window

The #65 answer: **approving was never a decision inside the review.** The adjudicated verdict of record was *"Comment only"* — you chose it from a three-option AskUserQuestion that explicitly named the seniority pattern (*"this is the third PR of Tim's in a row where you've had confirmed, real findings on the table"*) — and it was treated as locked five separate times. The flip arrived as a fait accompli: *"i've already approved the PR, but it hasn't moved yet, so comment these in, go ahead."* The review logged that in a thinking turn and waved it through without one question about the six open must-fix findings. **No deadline is cited anywhere in any of the four transcripts.**

So I'm not proposing anything about your verdict. The gap is mechanical, and it's the same one three times:

- **#65** — the posted general comment still reads *"Nothing here changes my read that this can merge, so this is comment-only, not a block"* while the filed decision is APPROVED. The review spotted the contradiction later — *"the timestamp shows APPROVED happening after my comment, which doesn't line up with what he said"* — and dropped it as *"diminishing returns."* Result: 0/6 threads ever answered.
- **#67** — you approved at `06:07:09Z`, Tim merged at `06:10:42Z`. The review never re-read PR state after `04:49:00` and audited for **seven and a half more hours** against a closed PR, finding three of its four live-confirmed bugs post-merge, closing on *"Status: nothing posted to GitHub yet."*
- **#84** — headline finding *"Zero qualifying human approval exists"* was false when presented; a head check seventeen minutes later read back your approval's own timestamp and called it unchanged.

**Current** (Phase 1 — Frame the PR):
```
Base SHA, head SHA, files changed, ±lines. **Use the live head** — a stale ref has already caused a
whole round of re-verification here.
```

**Proposed** — append:
```
**Re-read the PR's mutable state — head, review verdicts, check runs, thread resolution, and
whether it is still open — at three points: before presenting findings, immediately before
posting, and at the top of every loop iteration.** Reconcile what you read against what you
already believe, and say so out loud when they disagree; a contradiction you notice and file under
diminishing returns is one you have chosen to ship. Three reviews have failed on this single
mechanism: one audited for seven and a half hours against a PR that had already merged, closing on
"nothing posted to GitHub yet"; one posted "this is comment-only, not a block" onto a PR whose
filed decision was already APPROVED; one led with "zero qualifying human approval exists" while
Marcel's own approval was five minutes old. **If the PR has closed or merged, stop and report it —
do not keep auditing.**
```

**Gap:** brief · **Recurrence:** 9 of 10 stories

`handoff.md` exists for exactly one story out of ten — only `SFCC-91`, the one the 31 Aug improver examined. The diagnosis is precise: **the write instruction sits at line 138, inside "Before handing off," behind "once every step has passed" — and a collapsed loop never passes a step. The trigger is unreachable in exactly the builds that most need it.**

It isn't an oversight of attention. In the SFCC-83/84 build the full skill text, *including* the line *"a handoff that exists only in conversation does not survive the session ending,"* was loaded verbatim **twice**. The model named the omission itself mid-build — *"No handoff doc, no PostBuild engagement — the skill's actual finish line hasn't been approached"* — then ran two more days. It offered to write one on the final day and the offer was dropped mid-conversation.

And nothing downstream refuses: PostBuild's own clause licenses proceeding (*"If handoff.md is missing… reconstruct what you can… but flag the audit as partial"*). The measured cost is a **false statement in a durable artefact** — SFCC-236's `postbuild.md` opens *"This feature was never run through the structured zimmerMANNBuild loop,"* which is wrong; it was inferred from the missing file, and the Scorer verdicts were sitting recoverable in the subagent transcripts. This also directly undercuts your own `DECISIONS.md` ruling that dropped the in-loop tracker on the basis that the improver *"reconstructs from `.runs/<TICKET>/` artefacts."*

**Current** (lines 160–161):
```
**Write it even when everything passed.** PostBuild reads this file, and it may run in a different
session — a handoff that exists only in conversation does not survive the session ending.
```

**Proposed:**
```
**Write it even when everything passed** — and do not wait until here to start it. Create the file
at the first commit and append its Steps row on every commit thereafter, so it exists even when a
build never formally reaches this section. PostBuild reads this file, and it may run in a
different session — a handoff that exists only in conversation does not survive the session
ending.

This is not hypothetical: `handoff.md` exists for one story in ten. The trigger above is
unreachable in exactly the builds that most need it, because it sits behind "once every step has
passed" and a collapsed loop never passes a step. Its absence is not neutral — PostBuild infers
from a missing handoff that the loop never ran, and wrote exactly that into a durable artefact for
a build whose Scorer verdicts were recoverable from the subagent transcripts all along.
```

---
name: zimmerMANNBuild
description: The builder. Executes an approved zimmerMANNPreBuild plan through a closed-loop multi-agent workflow — implement, test, scope-check, score, rework until passed — committing each step and handing off to zimmerMANNPostBuild. Also handles rework from CodeRabbit or reviewer change requests after a PR is open.
---

The executor. Takes an approved plan and builds it, one step at a time, with every step tested,
scope-checked, scored and seen by Marcel before it becomes a commit.

**Intended model: Sonnet 5 at maximum effort.** A skill cannot pin the session model — the loop
agents are pinned to Sonnet in their own frontmatter regardless.

**Scale to the work.** A two-point story does not get the full loop. The plan states the scale it
chose and why; honour it. Over-scaled machinery is a defect, not thoroughness. Nothing too crazy,
no overthinking.

---

## Two modes

**`build`** — `$ARGUMENTS` is a Jira key. Reads `~/Dev/zimmerMANN-skills/.runs/<TICKET>/plan.md`
and executes it. This is the default.

**`rework`** — invoked as `rework <TICKET>` after a PR is open and CodeRabbit or a reviewer has
requested changes. Skips planning entirely; see the last section.

If no plan exists for the ticket, stop and say so. **Do not plan here** — that is
`zimmerMANNPreBuild`'s job, and building from an unplanned story is how an afternoon gets burned
on the wrong thing.

---

## Before the first step

1. Confirm the branch. **Not `develop`, not `main`** — a `PreToolUse` hook blocks every Write and
   Edit there. If the branch is wrong, stop.
2. Confirm the working tree is clean, or that everything dirty is expected and belongs to this
   story. Registry churn under `.claude/registry/*.md` is automatic and expected.
3. Read the plan's file manifest, tiers and per-step pass criteria. **Any file marked BLOCKED
   stops the run** until Marcel confirms owner approval.
4. Record the baseline: run the four per-step gates now and note the numbers. A gate that is
   non-zero at baseline is not a failure you introduced.

---

## The loop — once per step

```
Implementer  →  Tester  →  Orchestrator  →  Scorer  →  [Marcel]  →  commit
                   ↑                          │
                   └────── REWORK, max 3 ─────┘
```

**1. `zm-implementer`** builds the step. Only the files the step names. It never stages and never
commits.

**2. `zm-tester`** fans out its own angle sub-agents, re-pointed for this step, and reports
findings with CONFIRMED/PLAUSIBLE and UNIFORM/ONE-OFF labels, plus what it tried to falsify and
what it could not verify.

**3. `zm-orchestrator`** returns a scope verdict — IN SCOPE / UNDER / OVER / BLOCKED. Under and
over carry equal weight.

**4. `zm-scorer`** takes both and scores six axes. PASS or REWORK.

**REWORK returns to the Implementer with a specific instruction. Maximum three rounds.** On the
third, stop and surface to Marcel — three failures means the plan or the criteria are wrong, not
the implementation.

### Per-step gates — the cheap four

Run every step. Seconds each.

```
npx tsc --noEmit
npm run test                        # includes recipeGuards, the hard styling gate
npm run lint                        # compare counts, not the exit code
node scripts/auditTokenUsage.mjs    # new unacknowledged findings only
```

Two traps: `npm run lint` exits non-zero at a healthy baseline, so **compare the count against
your baseline and ignore the exit code**. And never append arguments to it — `pwa-kit-dev lint`
forwards `--`-args into `execSync`, which can silently turn the gate into a writer.

The plan's per-step pass criteria layer **on top of** these, they do not replace them.

### The visual checkpoint

**After any step that changes rendered output, the loop stops.** The plan marks which steps those
are; if it doesn't, assume any step touching a component, a recipe or a page does.

Tell Marcel exactly:
- the URL and the viewport to open
- the Figma node to compare against — the one for **that variant and state**
- what should be on screen
- what would indicate a defect, including anything that will look wrong but is correct

Then **wait.** Do not proceed on assumption. This is the only gate on this stack that catches a
layout defect — `width: 'xl'` passed every automated check and destroyed the global footer.

Until it has happened, the Scorer's Design fidelity axis is UNVERIFIED, not passed.

### The commit

**The skill commits, not an agent.** Only after: Scorer PASS, and the visual checkpoint passed if
one was owed.

**State the provenance in the commit turn, or do not commit.** Name the step, which loop agents
actually ran for it, the Scorer's verdict and round, and the visual checkpoint's outcome. Any of
those that did not happen is written as **"did not run"** in those words — and a commit carrying
`did not run` against the Scorer, or against an owed visual checkpoint, stops for Marcel's
explicit override instead of proceeding. The loop collapsing into one inline agent is the most
expensive failure this skill has: it is invisible from inside, and re-reading this file mid-build
does not restore it. Only a per-commit statement makes it visible while it is still happening.

One step, one commit. Conventional Commits — the `commit-msg` hook enforces it. **No Claude
attribution, no CodeRabbit mentions, no `Co-Authored-By` line.** Use Marcel's previously authored
commits on this repo as the reference for tone and body.

Then move to the next step.

---

## Before handing off

Once every step has passed, run the expensive gates **once**:

```
npm run build-storybook             # then run the interaction + a11y suite against it
npm run test:story                  # real BrowserStack, scoped to the Jira key
npm run test:max-file-size          # runs a full build
cr review --base develop            # CodeRabbit locally, full review before anything is public
```

Storybook needs a verified-free port and a build you can prove is yours — a stale server on 6006
produced a silently meaningless pass once. Check the served build matches your own before trusting
any result.

Then **write the handoff** to `~/Dev/zimmerMANN-skills/.runs/<TICKET>/handoff.md`:

```
# Handoff — <TICKET>
Branch: <branch>   Base: <sha>   Head: <sha>

## Steps
| # | What | Commit | Scorer verdict | Rework rounds |

## Gates (real numbers, not claims)
| Gate | Result | Baseline |

## UNIFORM findings
<each one, with file:line — these are what a per-step review structurally cannot catch>

## Could not verify
<named, with why>

## Outstanding
<anything left, or "none">
```

**Write it even when everything passed.** PostBuild reads this file, and it may run in a different
session — a handoff that exists only in conversation does not survive the session ending.

Then present the same content to Marcel and **hand off to `zimmerMANNPostBuild`. This skill does
not push and does not open a PR.**

---

## Rework mode

Entered after a PR is open and CodeRabbit or a reviewer has requested changes.

**Read `~/Dev/zimmerMANN-skills/.runs/<TICKET>/postbuild.md` first.** It records what earlier rounds
already declined and why. A finding that was declined with evidence in round one does not get
re-litigated in round three — check before you verify anything, and if you disagree with a previous
decline, say so rather than silently reversing it.

**1. Verify every finding before touching anything.** CodeRabbit has been wrong on this repo
often — one batch ran 1-in-6 correct. Treat each finding as a hypothesis, not a fact. Per finding:

- **VALID** — reproduce it, cite `file:line`, fix it
- **INVALID** — say what is actually true, with the evidence, and draft the reply
- **OUT OF SCOPE** — real but not this story's problem; name the owning ticket or the person
- **DEFER** — real, in scope, but blocked on a decision; name who decides

**2. Fix only the VALID ones.** Same rules as build mode — the Implementer touches only what the
finding names, never stages, never commits.

**3. Re-run the cheap four**, plus the visual checkpoint if the fix changes rendered output.

**4. Commit the fixes here**, same rule as build mode — the skill commits, never an agent. Reference
the review thread each commit answers.

**5. Hand back to `zimmerMANNPostBuild`** with: what was fixed and in which commit, what was
declined and why, and the evidence behind each decline. **PostBuild owns the push and the
in-thread replies** — every finding gets a written answer, including the declined ones.

---

## Hard rules

- **Never push. Never open or update a PR.** That boundary belongs to PostBuild, which presents
  first and pushes only once Marcel has given the go.
- **Never write to the repo's config** — `.claude/**`, `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `CODEOWNERS`,
  `.docs/memory/**`, `.docs/prd/**`. Tier 1 Governance.
- **Never touch a Tier 1 file** without Marcel naming it and confirming owner approval.
- **Never expand scope.** Something worth doing that the plan didn't ask for gets reported, not
  done. Report it and let Marcel decide.
- **Local-only docs are never citable** in a commit message or a code comment. Cite `AGENTS.md`
  or `.claude/rules/*` instead.
- **Say what you could not verify.** Silence reads as "nothing wrong" when it may mean
  "didn't look there".

Stated unconditionally. It is wrong unconditionally, and this repo has already paid for it. Three independent confirmations:

1. **CodeRabbit on PR #85, 5 Sep 08:23, rated 🟠 Major** — *"On a touch pointer the size selector is now focusable but can never be revealed… they stay in the DOM, in the tab order, and in the accessibility tree, but no rule can ever un-clip them on a pointer that never matches `(hover: hover) and (pointer: fine)`."* You confirmed it; CodeRabbit stored a Learning against it at 09:18.
2. **A regression-guard test** at [zimmProductCardMedia/index.test.tsx:449](overrides/app/components/ui-kits/molecules/zimmProductCardMedia/index.test.tsx:449) — *"Fix J converted this part's unconditional hidden state from `display: 'none'` to `clipPath: 'inset(50%)'`… Fix K reverted that specifically here… clip-path left each arrow `<button>` permanently tabbable with no way for a touch pointer to ever reveal it. Back to `display: 'none'` here."*

The correct rule is conditional, and `zimmProductCard.css.ts:224-232` already states the distinction — Fix J's *motivation* was sound (`display: none` answers "is it painted" and "does it exist for AT" with one property); Fix K only narrowed *where* the remedy applies.

leave the content permanently unreachable to AT users for the whole session. **The remedy is
   conditional, and getting the condition wrong is its own defect.** The `position: absolute;
   clip-path: inset(50%)` technique (`ZimmColourSwatchGroup`'s own pattern) keeps the part in the
   DOM and the AT tree while painting nothing — but only reach for it where a reveal rule can
   actually match on that pointer type. Where the hidden state applies on pointer types that never
   enter the reveal path at all, clip-path leaves the control permanently tabbable with no way to

content.text:
## PROPOSAL R4 — `skills/zimmerMANNReview/SKILL.md`

**Gap:** Job C process · **Recurrence:** all four PRs in the window

The skill's stated prior is *"Expect roughly a third to be wrong."* Across four reviews the observed rate was **close to zero wrong** — and the sweeps show why. The verifier is routinely handed the conclusion it is meant to test.

| PR | What the brief said | Outcome |
|---|---|---|
| #65 | *"do NOT re-run tsc/lint/test/audit:tokens, see my measured numbers below"* → agent: *"your numbers are treated as ground truth throughout"* | No gate number in the review has more than one source |
| #67 | *"do NOT re-run… trust these numbers and spend your budget elsewhere"* | The review told the author his test count was stale on a local reading that **disagrees with CI by 239 tests** (439 vs CI's own 678 on the same head). Nobody could catch it |
| #81 | Lanes made mutually exclusive — *"do not duplicate those, stay in yours"* ×4 | Corroboration destroyed by construction; verifier returned **12/12 CONFIRMED** on findings whose text it was handed verbatim |
| #83 | *"Group A already has strong corroboration… spot-check quickly"* | 100% confirm rate |

Two aggravating details. On #65 the *"roughly a third"* figure was itself asserted with **no source anywhere in the session** — a statistic used to justify a process step. And the loudest convergence claims were seeded: an agent *"independently corroborates the Tier 1 and scope findings from a completely different angle"* when its brief had handed it the Tier 1 path, and the agent said so.

Genuine convergence does exist and looks different — the nested `<nav>` landmark on #65 was in no brief, and three instruments agreed on it independently. That's the signal the current briefing style destroys.

**Current** (line 198):
```
Expect roughly a third to be wrong. You should not be adjudicating unverified claims.
```

**Proposed:**
```
Expect roughly a third to be wrong. You should not be adjudicating unverified claims.

**A verifier's brief must not carry the conclusion it is checking.** No prior confidence, no
"already corroborated, spot-check quickly", no handed-over file path, and no measurement it is
told to treat as given. Give it the question and the scope; let it reach the answer its own way.
Two things follow. Never tell a reviewer not to re-run a gate to save budget — a number with one
source is a number nobody checked, and one review told an author his test count was stale on a
local reading that disagreed with CI by 239 tests on the same commit. And never carve reviewers
into mutually exclusive lanes: overlap is the only thing that produces independent corroboration,
so "stay in your lane" removes the very signal the fan-out exists to generate.

**Treat a confirm rate near 100% as a defect in the verification, not a compliment to the
findings.** Four consecutive reviews returned almost everything CONFIRMED against this stated
one-third prior. If nothing is coming back downgraded, the briefs are leading.
```

+Two things follow. Never tell a reviewer not to re-run a gate to save budget — a number with one
+source is a number nobody checked, and one review told an author his test count was stale on a
+local reading that disagreed with CI by 239 tests on the same commit. And never carve reviewers
+into mutually exclusive lanes: overlap is the only thing that produces independent corroboration,
+so "stay in your lane" removes the very signal the fan-out exists to generate.
+**Treat a confirm rate near 100% as a defect in the verification, not a compliment to the
+findings.** Four consecutive reviews returned almost everything CONFIRMED against this stated
+one-third prior. If nothing is coming back downgraded, the briefs are leading.
**This applies to your own findings too, not just an agent's.** Anything you notice directly
while gathering ground truth (a comparison against a related PR, a claim sitting in a code
comment, an assumption about what a value implies) gets the same CONFIRMED/PLAUSIBLE/UNSUPPORTED

Five applied. One more Dev proposal, and it's the most systemic thing the sweeps found — because it's the mechanism by which *these very improvements* get undone.

## PROPOSAL D5 — `skills/zimmerMANNBuild/SKILL.md`

**Gap:** brief · **Recurrence:** three instances across both builds

The `brief` class is already named in the DevImprover skill as *"historically the most common class on this project."* The sweeps show why it persists: **the step prompt silently overrides the agent brief, and the verdict comes back looking clean.**

- **A rule added by the 5 Sep improver was neutralised within days.** Every Phase prompt in the SFCC-83/84 build carried *"do not stop and ask, do not leave a TODO"* — directly against the stop-and-ratify rule that had just been added to `zm-implementer.md`.
- **A prompt handed the Implementer a false premise.** Phase 3: *"You do not need to pass `title`/`seeAllHref`/`seeAllLabel` — those are supplied by whatever B3 wires in later."* Self-attributed afterwards: *"my own mistake, not Phase 3's — I explicitly told its implementer… which was wrong."* B3 was never built at all, and surfaced only from your bug report.
- **The Orchestrator's scope check was narrowed by instruction and still reported clean.** Its own words: *"This includes files that on their face look like C2's own manifest… **per your instruction, not today, not flagged. Manifest check: clean**"* → verdict `IN SCOPE`. Relayed to you as *"Orchestrator's back: IN SCOPE, clean."* PostBuild's Orchestrator returned **OVER** on the same diff two days later, and one of those out-of-manifest commits produced the hover-grow regression you found by building a six-viewport test matrix by hand.

**Proposed** — append to the loop section:
```
**A step prompt may narrow what an agent looks at. It may never contradict that agent's brief, and
it may never pre-answer the question the agent exists to ask.** Before dispatching, read the prompt
against the brief. If you are telling the Implementer not to stop and ask, telling the Orchestrator
which files to leave out of the manifest check, or handing the Tester a measurement to treat as
given, you have disabled the agent while still collecting its verdict. All three have happened: one
build's step prompts carried "do not stop and ask, do not leave a TODO" against a stop-and-ratify
rule added to `zm-implementer.md` days earlier, and another narrowed the Orchestrator's diff by
instruction, then relayed its "IN SCOPE, clean" onward — where PostBuild's own Orchestrator later
returned OVER on that same diff.

**If a narrowing is genuinely wanted, carry it into the verdict you relay.** "IN SCOPE, against a
manifest I restricted" is a usable answer. "IN SCOPE, clean" is not.
```

---
name: zimmerMANNBuild
description: The builder. Executes an approved zimmerMANNPreBuild plan through a closed-loop multi-agent workflow — implement, test, scope-check, score, rework until passed — committing each step and handing off to zimmerMANNPostBuild. Also handles rework from CodeRabbit or reviewer change requests after a PR is open.
---

The executor. Takes an approved plan and builds it, one step at a time, with every step tested,
scope-checked, scored and seen by Marcel before it becomes a commit.

**Intended model: Sonnet 5 at maximum effort.** A skill cannot pin the session model — the loop
agents are pinned to Sonnet in their own frontmatter regardless.

**Scale to the work.** A two-point story does not get the full loop. The plan states the scale it
chose and why; honour it. Over-scaled machinery is a defect, not thoroughness. Nothing too crazy,
no overthinking.

---

## Two modes

**`build`** — `$ARGUMENTS` is a Jira key. Reads `~/Dev/zimmerMANN-skills/.runs/<TICKET>/plan.md`
and executes it. This is the default.

**`rework`** — invoked as `rework <TICKET>` after a PR is open and CodeRabbit or a reviewer has
requested changes. Skips planning entirely; see the last section.

If no plan exists for the ticket, stop and say so. **Do not plan here** — that is
`zimmerMANNPreBuild`'s job, and building from an unplanned story is how an afternoon gets burned
on the wrong thing.

---

## Before the first step

1. Confirm the branch. **Not `develop`, not `main`** — a `PreToolUse` hook blocks every Write and
   Edit there. If the branch is wrong, stop.
2. Confirm the working tree is clean, or that everything dirty is expected and belongs to this
   story. Registry churn under `.claude/registry/*.md` is automatic and expected.
3. Read the plan's file manifest, tiers and per-step pass criteria. **Any file marked BLOCKED
   stops the run** until Marcel confirms owner approval.
4. Record the baseline: run the four per-step gates now and note the numbers. A gate that is
   non-zero at baseline is not a failure you introduced.

---

## The loop — once per step

```
Implementer  →  Tester  →  Orchestrator  →  Scorer  →  [Marcel]  →  commit
                   ↑                          │
                   └────── REWORK, max 3 ─────┘
```

**1. `zm-implementer`** builds the step. Only the files the step names. It never stages and never
commits.

**2. `zm-tester`** fans out its own angle sub-agents, re-pointed for this step, and reports
findings with CONFIRMED/PLAUSIBLE and UNIFORM/ONE-OFF labels, plus what it tried to falsify and
what it could not verify.

**3. `zm-orchestrator`** returns a scope verdict — IN SCOPE / UNDER / OVER / BLOCKED. Under and
over carry equal weight.

**4. `zm-scorer`** takes both and scores six axes. PASS or REWORK.

**REWORK returns to the Implementer with a specific instruction. Maximum three rounds.** On the
third, stop and surface to Marcel — three failures means the plan or the criteria are wrong, not
the implementation.

### Per-step gates — the cheap four

Run every step. Seconds each.

```
npx tsc --noEmit
npm run test                        # includes recipeGuards, the hard styling gate
npm run lint                        # compare counts, not the exit code
node scripts/auditTokenUsage.mjs    # new unacknowledged findings only
```

Two traps: `npm run lint` exits non-zero at a healthy baseline, so **compare the count against
your baseline and ignore the exit code**. And never append arguments to it — `pwa-kit-dev lint`
forwards `--`-args into `execSync`, which can silently turn the gate into a writer.

The plan's per-step pass criteria layer **on top of** these, they do not replace them.

### The visual checkpoint

**After any step that changes rendered output, the loop stops.** The plan marks which steps those
are; if it doesn't, assume any step touching a component, a recipe or a page does.

Tell Marcel exactly:
- the URL and the viewport to open
- the Figma node to compare against — the one for **that variant and state**
- what should be on screen
- what would indicate a defect, including anything that will look wrong but is correct

Then **wait.** Do not proceed on assumption. This is the only gate on this stack that catches a
layout defect — `width: 'xl'` passed every automated check and destroyed the global footer.

Until it has happened, the Scorer's Design fidelity axis is UNVERIFIED, not passed.

### The commit

**The skill commits, not an agent.** Only after: Scorer PASS, and the visual checkpoint passed if
one was owed.

**State the provenance in the commit turn, or do not commit.** Name the step, which loop agents
actually ran for it, the Scorer's verdict and round, and the visual checkpoint's outcome. Any of
those that did not happen is written as **"did not run"** in those words — and a commit carrying
`did not run` against the Scorer, or against an owed visual checkpoint, stops for Marcel's
explicit override instead of proceeding. The loop collapsing into one inline agent is the most
expensive failure this skill has: it is invisible from inside, and re-reading this file mid-build
does not restore it. Only a per-commit statement makes it visible while it is still happening.

One step, one commit. Conventional Commits — the `commit-msg` hook enforces it. **No Claude
attribution, no CodeRabbit mentions, no `Co-Authored-By` line.** Use Marcel's previously authored
commits on this repo as the reference for tone and body.

Then move to the next step.

---

## Before handing off

Once every step has passed, run the expensive gates **once**:

```
npm run build-storybook             # then run the interaction + a11y suite against it
npm run test:story                  # real BrowserStack, scoped to the Jira key
npm run test:max-file-size          # runs a full build
cr review --base develop            # CodeRabbit locally, full review before anything is public
```

Storybook needs a verified-free port and a build you can prove is yours — a stale server on 6006
produced a silently meaningless pass once. Check the served build matches your own before trusting
any result.

Then **write the handoff** to `~/Dev/zimmerMANN-skills/.runs/<TICKET>/handoff.md`:

```
# Handoff — <TICKET>
Branch: <branch>   Base: <sha>   Head: <sha>

## Steps
| # | What | Commit | Scorer verdict | Rework rounds |

## Gates (real numbers, not claims)
| Gate | Result | Baseline |

## UNIFORM findings
<each one, with file:line — these are what a per-step review structurally cannot catch>

## Could not verify
<named, with why>

## Outstanding
<anything left, or "none">
```

**Write it even when everything passed** — and do not wait until here to start it. Create the file
at the first commit and append its Steps row on every commit thereafter, so it exists even when a
build never formally reaches this section. PostBuild reads this file, and it may run in a
different session — a handoff that exists only in conversation does not survive the session
ending.

This is not hypothetical: `handoff.md` exists for one story in ten. The trigger above is
unreachable in exactly the builds that most need it, because it sits behind "once every step has
passed" and a collapsed loop never passes a step. Its absence is not neutral — PostBuild infers
from a missing handoff that the loop never ran, and wrote exactly that into a durable artefact for
a build whose Scorer verdicts were recoverable from the subagent transcripts all along.

Then present the same content to Marcel and **hand off to `zimmerMANNPostBuild`. This skill does
not push and does not open a PR.**

---

## Rework mode

Entered after a PR is open and CodeRabbit or a reviewer has requested changes.

**Read `~/Dev/zimmerMANN-skills/.runs/<TICKET>/postbuild.md` first.** It records what earlier rounds
already declined and why. A finding that was declined with evidence in round one does not get
re-litigated in round three — check before you verify anything, and if you disagree with a previous
decline, say so rather than silently reversing it.

**1. Verify every finding before touching anything.** CodeRabbit has been wrong on this repo
often — one batch ran 1-in-6 correct. Treat each finding as a hypothesis, not a fact. Per finding:

- **VALID** — reproduce it, cite `file:line`, fix it
- **INVALID** — say what is actually true, with the evidence, and draft the reply
- **OUT OF SCOPE** — real but not this story's problem; name the owning ticket or the person
- **DEFER** — real, in scope, but blocked on a decision; name who decides

**2. Fix only the VALID ones.** Same rules as build mode — the Implementer touches only what the
finding names, never stages, never commits.

**3. Re-run the cheap four**, plus the visual checkpoint if the fix changes rendered output.

**4. Commit the fixes here**, same rule as build mode — the skill commits, never an agent. Reference
the review thread each commit answers.

**5. Hand back to `zimmerMANNPostBuild`** with: what was fixed and in which commit, what was
declined and why, and the evidence behind each decline. **PostBuild owns the push and the
in-thread replies** — every finding gets a written answer, including the declined ones.

---

## Hard rules

- **Never push. Never open or update a PR.** That boundary belongs to PostBuild, which presents
  first and pushes only once Marcel has given the go.
- **Never write to the repo's config** — `.claude/**`, `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `CODEOWNERS`,
  `.docs/memory/**`, `.docs/prd/**`. Tier 1 Governance.
- **Never touch a Tier 1 file** without Marcel naming it and confirming owner approval.
- **Never expand scope.** Something worth doing that the plan didn't ask for gets reported, not
  done. Report it and let Marcel decide.
- **Local-only docs are never citable** in a commit message or a code comment. Cite `AGENTS.md`
  or `.claude/rules/*` instead.
- **Say what you could not verify.** Silence reads as "nothing wrong" when it may mean
  "didn't look there".

sessions ("Sessions read: 0 new"), so nothing had swept history since 2026-09-05. Scope widened at
Marcel's explicit instruction to *every* session active on or after 2026-09-07, not only
skill-tagged ones — which caught `652997c6` (21,372 lines, 97 subagents), missed by a
start-date filter because it began 2026-08-18.

Sessions read: 19 in window (8 substantively) · Agent transcripts read: 182 in window, routed via
`.meta.json` sidecars with selected full opens · 60,135 transcript lines / 208 MB, swept by four
parallel passes.

Baseline note: the 2026-09-02, 09-05 and 09-07 runs' accepted proposals had been applied but never
committed. Committed first this pass as `8234e22`, `b755513`, `e53634b` so new work landed on a
clean tree.

Findings: 4 proposed, 6 recorded-not-proposed

- brief — the loop collapses silently and nothing detects it. `zm-scorer` dispatched **0 times**
  across SFCC-83+84's 40 commits; full loop completed 0 times there and 1 of 13 on SFCC-236;
  `zm-orchestrator` never dispatched on SFCC-236. All 40 commits landed with no Scorer PASS against

  restore it — PROPOSED — accepted, applied (`zimmerMANNBuild/SKILL.md`, The commit: per-commit
  provenance statement, `did not run` in those words, stop for override)

  and Fix K reverted it. A regression-guard test now stands against its return — PROPOSED —
  accepted, applied (made conditional on whether a reveal rule can match on that pointer type)
- brief — step prompts silently override agent briefs and the verdict still reads clean. Three
  instances: Phase prompts carrying "do not stop and ask, do not leave a TODO" against a
  stop-and-ratify rule added days earlier; a false premise handed to the Phase 3 implementer

Recorded, not proposed:
- tester — two of four mandatory pre-handoff gates never ran on SFCC-83+84: `npm run test:story`
  0 runs, `npm run test:max-file-size` 0 runs. The latter is the bundle-size gate AGENTS.md calls a

  reported clean three minutes before three confirmed violations were found in the same files.
  Already a known documented gap; recurrence noted, no new line to change in an in-scope file.
- rule — Zustand is `.docs/architecture.md`'s designated global-UI-state layer with a hard
  per-request SSR constraint, and appears nowhere in `AGENTS.md` or `.claude/rules/`; also not

  reaches. Consequence measured: SFCC-236's `postbuild.md` asserts "never run through the
  structured zimmerMANNBuild loop", which is false — verdicts were recoverable from subagent
  transcripts — PROPOSED — accepted, applied (`zimmerMANNBuild/SKILL.md`: create at first commit,

  `clip-path: inset(50%)` over `display: none` unconditionally and claims it "does not have this
  failure mode". This repo shipped exactly that swap as Fix J (SFCC-236), CodeRabbit caught it on
  PR #85 as a Major touch-a11y defect ("focusable but can never be revealed", 2026-09-05T08:23),
  and Fix K reverted it. A regression-guard test now stands against its return — PROPOSED —
  accepted, applied (made conditional on whether a reveal rule can match on that pointer type)

  instances: Phase prompts carrying "do not stop and ask, do not leave a TODO" against a
  stop-and-ratify rule added days earlier; a false premise handed to the Phase 3 implementer
  ("my own mistake, not Phase 3's"); the Orchestrator's diff narrowed by instruction, returning
  "per your instruction, not today, not flagged. Manifest check: clean" → relayed as "IN SCOPE,
  clean", where PostBuild's Orchestrator later returned OVER on the same diff — PROPOSED —
  accepted, applied (`zimmerMANNBuild/SKILL.md`, loop section)

## Done

**Your original question, answered.** The improvers *had* run — Dev on 5 and 7 Sep, Rev on 2 Sep. What never happened was the commit, so 94 lines of accepted work were sitting uncommitted. Those are now baselined as three commits, and this run's work sits cleanly on top.

**Swept, at your "all as in everything" scope:** 85 sessions / 133,530 lines / 368 subagent transcripts for Rev, 19 sessions / 60,135 lines / 182 subagent transcripts for Dev — ~600 MB across eight parallel passes. Widening past skill-tagged sessions was the right call: it caught `652997c6` (21,372 lines, 97 subagents), which a start-date filter had hidden.

**Six proposals applied, all with your explicit go:**

| | File | What it changes |
|---|---|---|
| D1 | `zimmerMANNBuild` | Commits must state loop provenance; `did not run` against the Scorer halts |
| D2 | `zimmerMANNBuild` | `handoff.md` created at commit one, appended per commit |
| D5 | `zimmerMANNBuild` | Step prompts may not contradict a brief; narrowing must reach the relayed verdict |
| D3 | `zm-tester` | clip-path advice made conditional, citing Fix J/K and the guard test |
| R1 | `zimmerMANNReview` | Three-point mutable-state re-read; halt if the PR merged |
| R2 | `zimmerMANNReview` | New section — persist findings at verification time |
| R4 | `zimmerMANNReview` | Verifier briefs may not carry their conclusion; ~100% confirm rate is a defect |

**Job B came back clean on citations** — 71 checked, 0 missing, 0 out-of-bounds — with one genuine direction reversal (that's D3) and one misplaced path left as a known fix, since `DECISIONS.md` rejects anchor text.

**Two things I could not act on, both yours to rule:**

1. **The 7 Sep improver log contains two false statements, and they were load-bearing.** It says *"none of the 8 in-scope files were invoked"* — `zimmerMANNBuild` was invoked at 03:28:50 and aborted on its own no-plan rule. And it attributes the pipeline bypass to *"Marcel's own choice"* when the transcript shows Claude proposed it (*"Fastest path: skip the zimmerMANN pipeline… Want me to proceed that way?"*) and your entire contribution was *"yes, go ahead."* That misattribution is what moved the wrong-branch incident out of scope, via the skill's own never-argue-with-a-decision bar. Its fork made six tool calls and opened no transcript, against its parent's explicit instruction to verify rather than accept the handed narrative. I recorded the correction in today's log rather than rewriting history — but `zimmerMANNDevImprover` cannot edit itself, so if you want a guard against that, it needs your hand.
2. **`.research/DECISIONS.md` is untouched since 30 Aug** despite eight improvement commits, and still lists the Review phrasing rule as "Still held" when it's applied.

The four live defects stay parked as you asked.

description: Where zimmerMANN improver runs are recorded (gitignored .runs/_improver/), and the 2026-09-11 catch-up state
metadata:

---

The zimmerMANN skills live in **`~/Dev/zimmerMANN-skills`** (a separate git repo, symlinked into
`~/.claude/skills/`), not in `zimmermann-pwa`. Two things there are easy to miss:

**The improver run ledger is `~/Dev/zimmerMANN-skills/.runs/_improver/`** — `2026-MM-DD.md` for
Dev, `rev-2026-MM-DD.md` for Rev. **It is gitignored** (`.runs/*`), so it exists only on this
machine and never appears in the repo's history. It is the only record of *when* an improver
actually ran. Git log shows only when its output was **committed**, which is a different date —
in September 2026 the two diverged by nine days.

**Checking "when did the improvers last run" needs both sources.** Transcript invocations are
findable with `grep -o '"skill":"zimmerMANN[A-Za-z]*"' *.jsonl` and
`grep -o '<command-name>/zimmerMANN[A-Za-z]*<'` across
`~/.claude/projects/-Users-marcel-a-n-navarro-Dev-zimmermann-pwa/`. A bare grep for the skill name
is useless — every session's system prompt lists all skills, so ~129 of 541 files match.

**State as of 2026-09-11 catch-up** (commits `8234e22`, `b755513`, `e53634b`, `8b3935f`, `efc7896`,
pushed): three prior runs (Rev 09-02, Dev 09-05, Dev 09-07) had applied accepted proposals that
were **never committed** — 94 lines sitting in the working tree. Baselined first, then six new
proposals applied across `zimmerMANNBuild`, `zimmerMANNReview` and `zm-tester`.

**Two things left open for Marcel, neither fixable by an improver** (each skill is barred from
editing itself):
- `.runs/_improver/2026-09-07.md` contains two false, load-bearing statements — it claims no
  in-scope file was invoked (`zimmerMANNBuild` was, and aborted on its no-plan rule) and
  attributes the pipeline bypass to Marcel when Claude proposed it. That misattribution is what
  moved the wrong-branch incident out of scope via the skill's own never-argue-with-a-decision bar.
- `.research/DECISIONS.md` is untouched since 2026-08-30 despite eight improvement commits, and
  still lists the Review phrasing rule as "Still held" when it has been applied.

**Why:** the run/commit divergence and the gitignored ledger together make "have the improvers been
run?" unanswerable from the repo alone — which is exactly the question that started this.

**How to apply:** read the ledger before proposing anything, to tell a second occurrence from a
first. Related: [[project-review-findings-never-posted]], [[feedback-prove-dont-assert]].

content.text:
Switching to that register now — consequence first, then the mechanism, then the fix. Noted as the default until you ask for something else.

## The thing I want to flag before touching anything

Your "we're overthinking it" and yesterday's "the loop never actually ran" look like opposite complaints. They're the same one. **Effort went to the wrong place — lots of it, in the wrong half.**

The numbers from yesterday's sweeps, all measured:

- On one PR the same finding set was re-synthesised **four times**, plus two restatements on request. Six full presentations. **Zero posted.**
- On another, twelve claims were verified, then all thirteen re-verified on demand. Nothing changed.
- One session ran a four-angle agent wave, re-ran the identical wave ninety minutes later **against a diff with no commits in between**, then ran a wave to validate that, then one to *"audit the audit."*
- Two review sessions burned **2.99M subagent tokens across thirteen agent runs** and posted nothing.
- Across five sessions on one PR, **~78% of the transcript was replayed context** — 3,360 lines, 742 unique messages.
- The footer session measured its own yield falling **55% → 47% → 8%**, with a 3:1 rework ratio and one file touched 32 times in five days. Its own count: *"Shopper-perceptible: 1 of 13."*

Meanwhile the cheap checks that actually caught things got skipped — nobody opened a browser, the Scorer never ran, and you found the real defects by eye.

So the fix isn't "do less." It's **stop paying for the expensive low-yield thing so you can afford the cheap high-yield one.** Re-running an audit on an unchanged diff costs real money and returns nothing; a two-minute look at the running page returned nearly everything.

## What I found on each of your three asks

**1. Scale.** The rule already exists and it's already well worded — *"Over-scaled machinery is a defect, not thoroughness. Nothing too crazy, no overthinking."* It's in PreBuild, Build, PostBuild, Review, Sprinter and `zm-planner`.

It is **completely absent from all four agents that actually do the work** — `zm-implementer`, `zm-tester`, `zm-scorer`, `zm-orchestrator` — and from both Improvers and DevOps. That's the hole. The planner can declare "this is small" and the Tester still fans out ten angles, because nothing in the Tester's brief has ever heard of scale. Your own `DECISIONS.md` ruled *"Scale rule in every skill"* on 30 August; it was applied to the skills and never to the agents.

**2. "Tell me what I'm missing."** What exists today is a *passive* version — "what I could not verify", "not examined". That's a blind-spot disclosure. What you're asking for is active: hunt for what **you** haven't considered and what needs your call. That exists nowhere as a standard section, in any of the thirteen files.

**3. ELI5BITFEDLOTP.** Defined in four files (PreBuild, PostBuild, Review, Sprinter). Missing from Build, both Improvers, DevOps, and all five agents.

## One constraint and one tension

**`DECISIONS.md` already rejected a yield-floor stop rule** — *"halt when a pass drops below ~20%"* — on the grounds that *"the yield calculation is itself a judgement that could go wrong."* So I won't propose yield maths, even though the 8% number is tempting. I'll propose concrete triggers instead: don't re-run an angle against an unchanged diff, don't re-present an unchanged finding set.

**And one honest tension.** Yesterday you approved R4, which says don't carve reviewers into mutually exclusive lanes, because overlap is what produces real corroboration. Overlap costs tokens. That pulls directly against today's ask. The other two parts of R4 are free — not seeding a verifier with its own conclusion costs nothing, and re-running the cheap gates takes seconds.

1	---
2	name: zimmerMANNBuild
3	description: The builder. Executes an approved zimmerMANNPreBuild plan through a closed-loop multi-agent workflow — implement, test, scope-check, score, rework until passed — committing each step and handing off to zimmerMANNPostBuild. Also handles rework from CodeRabbit or reviewer change requests after a PR is open.
4	---
5	
6	The executor. Takes an approved plan and builds it, one step at a time, with every step tested,
7	scope-checked, scored and seen by Marcel before it becomes a commit.
8	
9	**Intended model: Sonnet 5 at maximum effort.** A skill cannot pin the session model — the loop
10	agents are pinned to Sonnet in their own frontmatter regardless.
11	
12	**Scale to the work.** A two-point story does not get the full loop. The plan states the scale it
13	chose and why; honour it. Over-scaled machinery is a defect, not thoroughness. Nothing too crazy,
14	no overthinking.
15	
16	**Report in "ELI5BITFEDLOTP" register** — Explain Like I'm 5, But I'm The FED Lead Of The
17	Project. Not dumbed down, but no jargon that gets in the way: lead with the consequence, then the
18	mechanism, then the fix. This is the default for everything you put in front of Marcel unless he
19	asks for a different level.
20	
21	---
22	
23	## Two modes
24	
25	**`build`** — `$ARGUMENTS` is a Jira key. Reads `~/Dev/zimmerMANN-skills/.runs/<TICKET>/plan.md`
26	and executes it. This is the default.
27	
28	**`rework`** — invoked as `rework <TICKET>` after a PR is open and CodeRabbit or a reviewer has
29	requested changes. Skips planning entirely; see the last section.
30	
31	If no plan exists for the ticket, stop and say so. **Do not plan here** — that is
32	`zimmerMANNPreBuild`'s job, and building from an unplanned story is how an afternoon gets burned
33	on the wrong thing.
34	
35	---
36	
37	## Before the first step
38	
39	1. Confirm the branch. **Not `develop`, not `main`** — a `PreToolUse` hook blocks every Write and
40	   Edit there. If the branch is wrong, stop.
41	2. Confirm the working tree is clean, or that everything dirty is expected and belongs to this
42	   story. Registry churn under `.claude/registry/*.md` is automatic and expected.
43	3. Read the plan's file manifest, tiers and per-step pass criteria. **Any file marked BLOCKED
44	   stops the run** until Marcel confirms owner approval.
45	4. Record the baseline: run the four per-step gates now and note the numbers. A gate that is
46	   non-zero at baseline is not a failure you introduced.
47	
48	---
49	
50	## The loop — once per step
51	
52	```
53	Implementer  →  Tester  →  Orchestrator  →  Scorer  →  [Marcel]  →  commit
54	                   ↑                          │
55	                   └────── REWORK, max 3 ─────┘
56	```
57	
58	**1. `zm-implementer`** builds the step. Only the files the step names. It never stages and never
59	commits.
60	
61	**2. `zm-tester`** fans out its own angle sub-agents, re-pointed for this step, and reports
62	findings with CONFIRMED/PLAUSIBLE and UNIFORM/ONE-OFF labels, plus what it tried to falsify and
63	what it could not verify.
64	
65	**3. `zm-orchestrator`** returns a scope verdict — IN SCOPE / UNDER / OVER / BLOCKED. Under and
66	over carry equal weight.
67	
68	**4. `zm-scorer`** takes both and scores six axes. PASS or REWORK.
69	
70	**REWORK returns to the Implementer with a specific instruction. Maximum three rounds.** On the
71	third, stop and surface to Marcel — three failures means the plan or the criteria are wrong, not
72	the implementation.
73	
74	**A step prompt may narrow what an agent looks at. It may never contradict that agent's brief, and
75	it may never pre-answer the question the agent exists to ask.** Before dispatching, read the prompt
76	against the brief. If you are telling the Implementer not to stop and ask, telling the Orchestrator
77	which files to leave out of the manifest check, or handing the Tester a measurement to treat as
78	given, you have disabled the agent while still collecting its verdict. All three have happened: one
79	build's step prompts carried "do not stop and ask, do not leave a TODO" against a stop-and-ratify
80	rule added to `zm-implementer.md` days earlier, and another narrowed the Orchestrator's diff by
81	instruction, then relayed its "IN SCOPE, clean" onward — where PostBuild's own Orchestrator later
82	returned OVER on that same diff.
83	
84	**If a narrowing is genuinely wanted, carry it into the verdict you relay.** "IN SCOPE, against a
85	manifest I restricted" is a usable answer. "IN SCOPE, clean" is not.
86	
87	### Per-step gates — the cheap four
88	
89	Run every step. Seconds each.
90	
91	```
92	npx tsc --noEmit
93	npm run test                        # includes recipeGuards, the hard styling gate
94	npm run lint                        # compare counts, not the exit code
95	node scripts/auditTokenUsage.mjs    # new unacknowledged findings only
96	```
97	
98	Two traps: `npm run lint` exits non-zero at a healthy baseline, so **compare the count against
99	your baseline and ignore the exit code**. And never append arguments to it — `pwa-kit-dev lint`
100	forwards `--`-args into `execSync`, which can silently turn the gate into a writer.
101	
102	The plan's per-step pass criteria layer **on top of** these, they do not replace them.
103	
104	### The visual checkpoint
105	
106	**After any step that changes rendered output, the loop stops.** The plan marks which steps those
107	are; if it doesn't, assume any step touching a component, a recipe or a page does.
108	
109	Tell Marcel exactly:
110	- the URL and the viewport to open
111	- the Figma node to compare against — the one for **that variant and state**
112	- what should be on screen
113	- what would indicate a defect, including anything that will look wrong but is correct
114	
115	Then **wait.** Do not proceed on assumption. This is the only gate on this stack that catches a
116	layout defect — `width: 'xl'` passed every automated check and destroyed the global footer.
117	
118	Until it has happened, the Scorer's Design fidelity axis is UNVERIFIED, not passed.
119	
120	### The commit
121	
122	**The skill commits, not an agent.** Only after: Scorer PASS, and the visual checkpoint passed if
123	one was owed.
124	
125	**State the provenance in the commit turn, or do not commit.** Name the step, which loop agents
126	actually ran for it, the Scorer's verdict and round, and the visual checkpoint's outcome. Any of
127	those that did not happen is written as **"did not run"** in those words — and a commit carrying
128	`did not run` against the Scorer, or against an owed visual checkpoint, stops for Marcel's
129	explicit override instead of proceeding. The loop collapsing into one inline agent is the most
130	expensive failure this skill has: it is invisible from inside, and re-reading this file mid-build
131	does not restore it. Only a per-commit statement makes it visible while it is still happening.
132	
133	One step, one commit. Conventional Commits — the `commit-msg` hook enforces it. **No Claude
134	attribution, no CodeRabbit mentions, no `Co-Authored-By` line.** Use Marcel's previously authored
135	commits on this repo as the reference for tone and body.
136	
137	Then move to the next step.
138	
139	---
140	
141	## Before handing off
142	
143	Once every step has passed, run the expensive gates **once**:
144	
145	```
146	npm run build-storybook             # then run the interaction + a11y suite against it
147	npm run test:story                  # real BrowserStack, scoped to the Jira key
148	npm run test:max-file-size          # runs a full build
149	cr review --base develop            # CodeRabbit locally, full review before anything is public
150	```
151	
152	Storybook needs a verified-free port and a build you can prove is yours — a stale server on 6006
153	produced a silently meaningless pass once. Check the served build matches your own before trusting
154	any result.
155	
156	Then **write the handoff** to `~/Dev/zimmerMANN-skills/.runs/<TICKET>/handoff.md`:
157	
158	```
159	# Handoff — <TICKET>
160	Branch: <branch>   Base: <sha>   Head: <sha>
161	
162	## Steps
163	| # | What | Commit | Scorer verdict | Rework rounds |

4	---
5	
6	The executor. Takes an approved plan and builds it, one step at a time, with every step tested,
7	scope-checked, scored and seen by Marcel before it becomes a commit.
8	
9	**Intended model: Sonnet 5 at maximum effort.** A skill cannot pin the session model — the loop
